def _json_bytes(value: object) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
                      ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8")


def sha256_file(path: Path | str) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with Path(path).open("rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(4 * 1024 * 1024), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def _source(path: Path | str, role: str) -> dict:
    p = Path(path).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
    if not p.is_file():
        raise LedgerError(f"Not a regular input file: {p}")
    return {"role": role, "path": str(p), "bytes": p.stat().st_size,
            "sha256": sha256_file(p)}


def atomic_json(path: Path, value: object) -> None:
    temp = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
    with temp.open("wb") as f:
        f.write(_json_bytes(value)); f.flush(); os.fsync(f.fileno())
    temp.replace(path)


def load_zones(path: Path | str, target_crs: CRS, *, id_field: str = "huc12",
               name_field: str = "name", zone_crs: str | None = None) -> list[Zone]:
    """Load GeoJSON, retaining identifier strings, multipart geometry and holes."""
    data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    if data.get("type") != "FeatureCollection" or not data.get("features"):
        raise LedgerError("Zones must be a nonempty GeoJSON FeatureCollection")
    declared = (data.get("crs") or {}).get("properties", {}).get("name")
    source_crs = CRS.from_user_input(zone_crs or declared or "EPSG:4326")
    xform = Transformer.from_crs(source_crs, target_crs, always_xy=True).transform
    zones, seen = [], set()
    for i, feature in enumerate(data["features"]):
        props = feature.get("properties") or {}
        zid = props.get(id_field)
        if zid is None or isinstance(zid, (dict, list, bool)):
            raise LedgerError(f"Feature {i} has no scalar {id_field!r}")
        # HUC identifiers must arrive as strings: numeric JSON can destroy zeros.
        if "huc" in id_field.lower() and not isinstance(zid, str):
            raise LedgerError(f"Feature {i}: {id_field} must be a string")
        zid = str(zid)
        if not zid or zid == "__domain__" or zid in seen:
            raise LedgerError(f"Empty, reserved or duplicate zone id: {zid!r}")
        geom = shape(feature.get("geometry"))
        if geom.geom_type not in ("Polygon", "MultiPolygon") or geom.is_empty:
            raise LedgerError(f"Zone {zid}: nonempty polygon geometry required")
        if not geom.is_valid:
            raise LedgerError(f"Zone {zid}: invalid geometry: {shapely.is_valid_reason(geom)}")
        if source_crs != target_crs:
            geom = geometry_transform(xform, geom)
        if not geom.is_valid or not np.isfinite(geom.bounds).all() or geom.area <= 0:
            raise LedgerError(f"Zone {zid}: unusable geometry after reprojection")
        seen.add(zid)
        zones.append(Zone(zid, str(props.get(name_field) or zid), geom))
    return zones


def _footprint(transform, height: int, width: int):
    return Polygon([transform * p for p in ((0, 0), (width, 0),
                                            (width, height), (0, height))])


def _pixel_polygons(rows: np.ndarray, cols: np.ndarray, transform):
    corners = np.array([[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1]], dtype=np.float64)
    xy = np.stack((cols, rows), axis=1)[:, None, :] + corners[None, :, :]
    world = np.empty_like(xy)
    world[..., 0] = transform.a * xy[..., 0] + transform.b * xy[..., 1] + transform.c
    world[..., 1] = transform.d * xy[..., 0] + transform.e * xy[..., 1] + transform.f
    return shapely.polygons(world)


def coverage_weights(geometry, transform, height: int, width: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return polygon intersection / cell area, including slivers and holes.

    Full interior cells use rasterization. Boundary and adjacent cells use exact
    planar intersections (floating-point GEOS), never center-count area estimates.
    An area-conservation check falls back to intersection of all touched cells.
    """
    footprint = _footprint(transform, height, width)
    clipped = geometry.intersection(footprint)
    weights = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.float64)
    if clipped.is_empty or clipped.area == 0:
        return weights
    if geometry.covers(footprint):
        weights.fill(1.0)
        return weights
    if clipped.geom_type == "GeometryCollection":
        clipped = shapely.union_all([part for part in shapely.get_parts(clipped) if part.area > 0])
    cell_area = abs(transform.a * transform.e - transform.b * transform.d)
    weights[:] = rasterize([(mapping(clipped), 1)], out_shape=weights.shape,
                           transform=transform, dtype="uint8")
    border = rasterize([(mapping(clipped.boundary), 1)], out_shape=weights.shape,
                       transform=transform, all_touched=True, dtype="uint8").astype(bool)
    # Expanding one cell handles coincident edges and rasterizer rounding.
    padded = np.pad(border, 1)
    nearby = np.zeros_like(border)
    for dr in range(3):
        for dc in range(3):
            nearby |= padded[dr:dr + height, dc:dc + width]
    rows, cols = np.nonzero(nearby)
    if len(rows):
        values = shapely.area(shapely.intersection(_pixel_polygons(rows, cols, transform), clipped))
        weights[rows, cols] = np.clip(values / cell_area, 0.0, 1.0)
    tolerance = max(1e-6, clipped.area * 2e-10)
    if abs(weights.sum(dtype=np.float64) * cell_area - clipped.area) > tolerance:
        touched = rasterize([(mapping(clipped), 1)], out_shape=weights.shape,
                            transform=transform, all_touched=True, dtype="uint8")
        rows, cols = np.nonzero(touched)
        weights.fill(0.0)
        values = shapely.area(shapely.intersection(_pixel_polygons(rows, cols, transform), clipped))
        weights[rows, cols] = np.clip(values / cell_area, 0.0, 1.0)
        if abs(weights.sum() * cell_area - clipped.area) > tolerance:
            raise LedgerError("Polygon/pixel area conservation failed; check coordinate precision")
    return weights


def _grid_info(dataset, allow_projected_area: bool) -> dict:
    if dataset.crs is None:
        raise LedgerError("Baseline raster has no CRS")
    crs = CRS.from_user_input(dataset.crs)
    if not crs.is_projected or len(crs.axis_info) < 2:
        raise LedgerError("Use the original projected equal-area grid, not longitude/latitude cells")
    scale = crs.axis_info[0].unit_conversion_factor
    if not math.isclose(scale, crs.axis_info[1].unit_conversion_factor):
        raise LedgerError("Grid axes have inconsistent linear units")
    method = crs.coordinate_operation.method_name if crs.coordinate_operation else ""
    equal_area = "equal area" in method.lower() or "equal-area" in method.lower()
    if not equal_area and not allow_projected_area:
        raise LedgerError(f"CRS method {method!r} is not equal-area; use the native EPSG:5070 grid")
    determinant = abs(dataset.transform.a * dataset.transform.e - dataset.transform.b * dataset.transform.d)
    if not math.isfinite(determinant) or determinant <= 0:
        raise LedgerError("Invalid grid transform")
    return {"crs": crs.to_string(), "wkt": crs.to_wkt(),
            "width": dataset.width, "height": dataset.height,
            "transform": list(dataset.transform)[:6], "cell_ha": determinant * scale**2 / 10000,
            "coordinate_unit_to_m": scale, "area_basis": "equal-area projection" if equal_area else "projected planar area",
            "projection_method": method}


def _read_classes(dataset, spec: RasterInput, window: Window, domain_mask: np.ndarray,
                  unknown_policy: str):
    raw = dataset.read(spec.band, window=window)
    source_valid = dataset.read_masks(spec.band, window=window) != 0
    supported = source_valid & np.isin(raw, CODES)
    unknown = source_valid & ~supported & domain_mask
    if unknown.any() and unknown_policy == "error":
        codes, counts = np.unique(raw[unknown], return_counts=True)
        raise LedgerError(f"Unsupported NLCD classes inside study area in {spec.path}: "
                          + str(dict(zip(codes.tolist(), counts.tolist()))))
    # All unsupported values receive index 0 solely as an unused placeholder.
    safe = np.where(supported, raw, CODES[0]).astype(np.uint8)
    return safe, LUT[safe], source_valid, supported, raw


def _delta(weights: np.ndarray, base, scenario, all_valid: np.ndarray,
           pixel_ha: float, support_scope: str) -> dict:
    _, bi, bv, bs, br = base
    _, si, sv, ss, sr = scenario
    active = weights > 0
    pair = bs & ss
    analysis = pair if support_scope == "pair" else all_valid
    mask = active & analysis
    weighted = weights * pixel_ha
    area = lambda m: float(weighted[m].sum(dtype=np.float64))
    support = dict(zip(SUPPORT_KEYS, [
        float(weighted.sum()), area(bv), area(sv), area(bs), area(ss),
        area(pair), area(analysis), area(bs & ~ss), area(ss & ~bs),
        area(~bs & ~ss), area(pair & ~analysis), area(bv & ~bs), area(sv & ~ss),
    ]))
    encoded = bi[mask].astype(np.int32) * N_CLASSES + si[mask]
    matrix = np.bincount(encoded, weights=weighted[mask], minlength=N_CLASSES**2)
    cells = np.bincount(encoded, minlength=N_CLASSES**2)
    nonzero = np.flatnonzero(cells)
    transitions = [[int(i), float(matrix[i]), int(cells[i])] for i in nonzero]
    unknowns = {}
    for side, raw, source_valid, supported in (("baseline", br, bv, bs), ("scenario", sr, sv, ss)):
        unknown_mask = active & source_valid & ~supported
        if unknown_mask.any():
            codes, inv = np.unique(raw[unknown_mask], return_inverse=True)
            hectares = np.bincount(inv, weights=weighted[unknown_mask])
            unknowns[side] = {str(int(c)): float(a) for c, a in zip(codes, hectares)}
    return {"support": support, "transitions": transitions, "unknown_classes_ha": unknowns}


def _slug(name: str) -> str:
    stem = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]+", "-", name).strip("-")[:60] or "scenario"
    return stem + "-" + hashlib.sha256(name.encode()).hexdigest()[:10]


@contextmanager
def _exclusive_lock(path: Path):
    import fcntl
    with path.open("a+b") as f:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError as exc:
            raise LedgerError("Another process is already writing this ledger") from exc
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_UN)


def _initialize_raster(path: Path, baseline, dtype: str, description: str, nodata=0):
    profile = {"driver": "GTiff", "width": baseline.width, "height": baseline.height,
               "count": 1, "crs": baseline.crs, "transform": baseline.transform,
               "dtype": dtype, "nodata": nodata, "compress": "deflate",
               "tiled": True, "blockxsize": 256, "blockysize": 256,
               "BIGTIFF": "IF_SAFER"}
    with rasterio.open(path, "w", **profile) as out:
        out.set_band_description(1, description)
        out.update_tags(ledger_schema=SCHEMA, ledger_version=VERSION)


def _write_window(path: Path, data: np.ndarray, window: Window) -> None:
    # Closing before the SQLite commit is essential for process-death recovery.
    # A crash before commit causes deterministic overwrite of the same window.
    with rasterio.open(path, "r+") as target:
        target.write(data, 1, window=window)


def _aggregate(db: sqlite3.Connection, zone_meta: list[dict], scenario_names: list[str],
               config: dict, grid: dict, complete: bool) -> dict:
    accum = {}
    for zone in zone_meta:
        for scenario in scenario_names:
            accum[(zone["id"], scenario)] = {
                "support": dict.fromkeys(SUPPORT_KEYS, 0.0),
                "matrix": np.zeros((N_CLASSES, N_CLASSES), dtype=np.float64),
                "cells": np.zeros((N_CLASSES, N_CLASSES), dtype=np.int64), "unknown": {},
            }
    for (payload,) in db.execute("SELECT payload FROM tiles ORDER BY tile_id"):
        items = json.loads(zlib.decompress(payload))
        for item in items:
            a = accum[(item["zone_id"], item["scenario"])]
            for key, value in item["support"].items():
                a["support"][key] += value
            for index, hectares, cells in item["transitions"]:
                row, col = divmod(index, N_CLASSES)
                a["matrix"][row, col] += hectares; a["cells"][row, col] += cells
            for side, unknown in item["unknown_classes_ha"].items():
                for code, hectares in unknown.items():
                    key = side + ":" + code
                    a["unknown"][key] = a["unknown"].get(key, 0.0) + hectares
    rows = []
    for zone in zone_meta:
        for scenario in scenario_names:
            a = accum[(zone["id"], scenario)]
            matrix, support = a["matrix"], a["support"]
            common = float(matrix.sum())
            if complete and not math.isclose(support["covered_ha"], zone["inside_grid_ha"], rel_tol=3e-9, abs_tol=1e-7):
                raise LedgerError(f"Zone coverage does not conserve area: {zone['id']}")
            if not math.isclose(common, support["analysis_valid_ha"], rel_tol=3e-10, abs_tol=1e-8):
                raise LedgerError("Transition matrix/support mismatch")
            transitions = []
            for i, j in zip(*np.nonzero(a["cells"])):
                transitions.append({"from_code": int(CODES[i]), "to_code": int(CODES[j]),
                                    "ha": float(matrix[i, j]),
                                    "intersecting_cells": int(a["cells"][i, j])})
            groups = {}
            for group, codes in GROUPS.items():
                indices = [int(LUT[c]) for c in codes]
                before = float(matrix[indices, :].sum()); after = float(matrix[:, indices].sum())
                retained = float(matrix[np.ix_(indices, indices)].sum())
                groups[group] = {"baseline_ha": before, "scenario_ha": after,
                                 "gained_ha": max(0.0, after - retained), "lost_ha": max(0.0, before - retained),
                                 "net_ha": after - before}
                if not common:
                    groups[group] = dict.fromkeys(groups[group], None)
            unchanged = float(np.trace(matrix))
            changed = float(matrix[~np.eye(N_CLASSES, dtype=bool)].sum())
            rows.append({"zone_id": zone["id"], "zone_name": zone["name"], "scenario": scenario,
                         "support": support, "changed_ha": changed if common else None,
                         "unchanged_ha": unchanged if common else None,
                         "changed_pct_of_analysis": changed / common * 100 if common else None,
                         "analysis_coverage_pct": common / zone["inside_grid_ha"] * 100 if zone["inside_grid_ha"] else None,
                         "groups": groups, "transitions": transitions,
                         "unknown_classes_ha": a["unknown"]})
    return {"schema": SCHEMA, "version": VERSION, "complete": complete,
            "title": config["options"]["title"], "grid": grid, "inputs": config["sources"],
            "options": config["options"], "zones": zone_meta, "scenarios": scenario_names,
            "classes": {str(k): v for k, v in CLASSES.items()}, "rows": rows,
            "interpretation": [
                "Class-change hectares describe land-cover transitions, not modeled runoff, temperature, cost, or benefit.",
                "Baseline/scenario class areas share the selected analysis mask; nodata is accounted separately.",
                "Boundary area is polygon/pixel intersection in the reported projection; land-cover attribution remains at source pixel resolution.",
                "Intersecting-cell counts count positive-area touches; use hectares, not cell counts, when summing watershed boundaries.",
                "Domain rows use the unique union; overlapping zone rows must not be summed." if config["options"]["allow_overlap"] else "Watersheds have disjoint positive-area interiors; domain rows are their unique union.",
            ]}


def run_ledger(baseline: RasterInput, scenarios: Mapping[str, RasterInput],
               zones_path: Path | str, output: Path | str, *, options: Options | None = None,
               id_field: str = "huc12", name_field: str = "name", zone_crs: str | None = None,
               context_files: Sequence[Path | str] = (),
               temporal_years: Sequence[int] | None = None,
               progress: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None) -> dict:
    """Compute a complete retained ledger. Resume repeats only uncommitted tiles.

    Inputs are local native raster editions; grid mismatches fail without resampling.
    Output is a new directory, or the same checkpoint directory with resume=True.
    Callbacks run after a tile commit and may cancel by raising an exception.
    """
    options = options or Options()
    if not scenarios or any(not isinstance(k, str) or not k.strip() for k in scenarios):
        raise LedgerError("At least one named scenario raster is required")
    if not isinstance(options.tile_size, int) or options.tile_size < 1:
        raise LedgerError("tile_size must be a positive integer")
    if options.support_scope not in ("all", "pair") or options.unknown_policy not in ("error", "exclude"):
        raise LedgerError("Unknown support_scope or unknown_policy")
    temporal = None
    if temporal_years is not None:
        from . import landcover_temporal as temporal
        temporal_years = temporal.years(temporal_years, len(scenarios) + 1)
        if options.support_scope != "all":
            raise LedgerError("Temporal accounting requires common support across all observations")
    output = Path(output).expanduser().resolve()
    sources = [_source(baseline.path, "baseline"), _source(zones_path, "zones")]
    sources += [_source(spec.path, "scenario:" + name) for name, spec in scenarios.items()]
    sources += [_source(p, "context") for p in context_files]
    # GDAL validity may live in .msk or auxiliary files. Hash every local dataset
    # dependency, including VRT source files, not just the primary TIFF bytes.
    seen_paths = {record["path"] for record in sources}
    for spec in [baseline, *scenarios.values()]:
        with rasterio.open(Path(spec.path)) as dataset:
            for dependency in dataset.files:
                dep = str(Path(dependency).expanduser().resolve(strict=True))
                if dep not in seen_paths:
                    sources.append(_source(dep, "raster-companion"))
                    seen_paths.add(dep)
    if any(Path(s["path"]).is_relative_to(output) for s in sources):
        raise LedgerError("Output directory must not contain input files")
    fingerprint_options = {key: value for key, value in vars(options).items() if key != "resume"}
    config = {"schema": SCHEMA, "version": VERSION, "sources": sources,
              "options": fingerprint_options, "id_field": id_field, "name_field": name_field,
              "zone_crs": zone_crs, "baseline_band": baseline.band,
              "scenario_bands": {k: v.band for k, v in scenarios.items()},
              "scenario_order": list(scenarios)}
    if temporal is not None:
        config["temporal"] = {"schema": temporal.SCHEMA, "years": temporal_years,
                              "reducer_sha256": sha256_file(temporal.__file__)}
    signature = hashlib.sha256(_json_bytes(config)).hexdigest()
    if output.exists() and not options.resume:
        raise LedgerError(f"Output already exists; use --resume or a new output: {output}")
    if options.resume and not (output / "ledger.sqlite3").is_file():
        raise LedgerError("Resume requires an existing ledger.sqlite3 checkpoint")
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with _exclusive_lock(output / ".writer.lock"), ExitStack() as stack:
        specs = [baseline, *scenarios.values()]
        datasets = [stack.enter_context(rasterio.open(Path(s.path))) for s in specs]
        source = datasets[0]
        grid = _grid_info(source, options.allow_projected_area)
        for spec, dataset in zip(specs, datasets):
            if (dataset.width, dataset.height, dataset.crs, dataset.transform) != (source.width, source.height, source.crs, source.transform):
                raise LedgerError(f"Native grid mismatch: {spec.path}")
            if not isinstance(spec.band, int) or not 1 <= spec.band <= dataset.count:
                raise LedgerError(f"Invalid band {spec.band} for {spec.path}")
            if not np.issubdtype(np.dtype(dataset.dtypes[spec.band - 1]), np.integer):
                raise LedgerError(f"Categorical land cover requires an integer raster band: {spec.path}")
        zones = load_zones(zones_path, CRS.from_user_input(source.crs), id_field=id_field,
                           name_field=name_field, zone_crs=zone_crs)
        tree = STRtree([z.geometry for z in zones])
        if not options.allow_overlap:
            for i, zone in enumerate(zones):
                for j in tree.query(zone.geometry, predicate="intersects"):
                    if int(j) > i and zone.geometry.intersection(zones[int(j)].geometry).area > 1e-7:
                        raise LedgerError(f"Overlapping zone interiors: {zone.id} / {zones[int(j)].id}")
        domain = shapely.union_all([z.geometry for z in zones])
        footprint = _footprint(source.transform, source.height, source.width)
        if domain.intersection(footprint).area <= 0:
            raise LedgerError("No positive-area intersection between watersheds and raster grid")
        factor = grid["coordinate_unit_to_m"]**2 / 10000
        zone_meta = []
        for zone in [Zone("__domain__", "Study area union", domain), *zones]:
            total, inside = zone.geometry.area * factor, zone.geometry.intersection(footprint).area * factor
            zone_meta.append({"id": zone.id, "name": zone.name, "geometry_ha": total,
                              "inside_grid_ha": inside, "outside_grid_ha": max(0.0, total - inside)})
        db = sqlite3.connect(output / "ledger.sqlite3")
        stack.callback(db.close)
        db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE"); db.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=FULL")
        db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)")
        db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tiles (tile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, payload BLOB NOT NULL)")
        old = db.execute("SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key='signature'").fetchone()
        if old and not options.resume:
            raise LedgerError("Another writer already created this edition; use --resume or a new output")
        if old and old[0] != signature:
            raise LedgerError("Input bytes, band selection or ledger options changed; create a new edition")
        if not old:
            if options.resume:
                raise LedgerError("Checkpoint has no original input signature")
            db.executemany("INSERT INTO meta VALUES (?,?)", [("signature", signature), ("config", _json_bytes(config).decode()), ("grid", _json_bytes(grid).decode())])
            db.commit()
        names = list(scenarios)
        paths = {name: output / ("transition-" + _slug(name) + ".tif") for name in names}
        fraction_path = output / "study-area-fraction.tif"
        if options.write_rasters:
            for p, dtype, description in [(fraction_path, "float64", "Unique study-area polygon fraction per native pixel"), *[(p, "uint16", "NLCD baseline * 100 + scenario; zero is excluded") for p in paths.values()]]:
                if not options.resume:
                    _initialize_raster(p, source, dtype, description)
                elif not p.is_file():
                    raise LedgerError(f"Checkpoint raster missing: {p}; use a new output edition")
        temporal_paths = (temporal.initialize_rasters(output, source, temporal_years, options.resume)
                          if temporal is not None and options.write_rasters else {})
        windows = [(r, c, min(options.tile_size, source.height-r), min(options.tile_size, source.width-c))
                   for r in range(0, source.height, options.tile_size)
                   for c in range(0, source.width, options.tile_size)]
        completed = {row[0] for row in db.execute("SELECT tile_id FROM tiles")}
        atomic_json(output / "status.json", {"signature": signature, "state": "running", "completed_tiles": len(completed), "total_tiles": len(windows)})
        for tile_id, (row, col, height, width) in enumerate(windows):
            if tile_id in completed:
                continue
            window = Window(col, row, width, height)
            transform = source.window_transform(window)
            tile_footprint = _footprint(transform, height, width)
            candidates = tree.query(tile_footprint, predicate="intersects")
            zone_weights = []
            domain_weights = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.float64)
            for index in sorted(int(i) for i in candidates):
                zone = zones[index]
                weights = coverage_weights(zone.geometry, transform, height, width)
                if weights.any():
                    zone_weights.append((zone.id, weights)); domain_weights += weights
            if options.allow_overlap and len(zone_weights) > 1:
                domain_weights = coverage_weights(domain, transform, height, width)
            else:
                if domain_weights.max(initial=0) > 1 + 1e-9:
                    raise LedgerError("Watershed fractions exceed unique domain area")
                np.clip(domain_weights, 0, 1, out=domain_weights)
            deltas = []
            prepared_temporal = None
            values = None
            if domain_weights.any():
                values = [_read_classes(ds, spec, window, domain_weights > 0, options.unknown_policy)
                          for ds, spec in zip(datasets, specs)]
                all_valid = np.logical_and.reduce([v[3] for v in values])
                if temporal is not None:
                    prepared_temporal = temporal.prepare_tile(values, all_valid & (domain_weights > 0), temporal_years)
                for zid, weights in [("__domain__", domain_weights), *zone_weights]:
                    for name, scenario_values in zip(names, values[1:]):
                        delta = _delta(weights, values[0], scenario_values, all_valid,
                                       grid["cell_ha"], options.support_scope)
                        delta.update(zone_id=zid, scenario=name)
                        if temporal is not None and name == names[0]:
                            delta["temporal"] = temporal.tile_delta(prepared_temporal, weights, grid["cell_ha"])
                        deltas.append(delta)
                if options.write_rasters:
                    for name, scenario_values in zip(names, values[1:]):
                        valid = (values[0][3] & scenario_values[3]) if options.support_scope == "pair" else all_valid
                        code = values[0][0].astype(np.uint16) * 100 + scenario_values[0]
                        code[~(valid & (domain_weights > 0))] = 0
                        _write_window(paths[name], code, window)
            elif options.write_rasters:
                for path in paths.values():
                    _write_window(path, np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint16), window)
            if temporal_paths:
                temporal.write_rasters(temporal_paths, values, prepared_temporal, window, (height, width))
            if options.write_rasters:
                _write_window(fraction_path, domain_weights, window)
            # The complete per-window aggregate is the transaction. No mutable
            # cumulative counters can be doubled by a repeated interrupted tile.
            db.execute("INSERT INTO tiles VALUES (?,?)", (tile_id, zlib.compress(_json_bytes(deltas), 6)))
            db.commit()
            completed.add(tile_id)
            status = {"signature": signature, "state": "running", "completed_tiles": len(completed), "total_tiles": len(windows)}
            atomic_json(output / "status.json", status)
            if progress:
                progress(status)
        # Verify retained raster/context inputs did not change during the computation.
        for record in sources:
            if sha256_file(record["path"]) != record["sha256"]:
                raise LedgerError(f"Input changed during run: {record['path']}; create a new edition")
        report = _aggregate(db, zone_meta, names, config, grid, True)
        report["signature"] = signature
        if temporal is not None:
            report["timeline"] = temporal.aggregate(db, report, temporal_years)
        to_wgs84 = Transformer.from_crs(source.crs, "EPSG:4326", always_xy=True).transform
        geojson = {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [
            {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"zone_id": z.id, "zone_name": z.name},
             "geometry": mapping(geometry_transform(to_wgs84, z.geometry))} for z in zones]}
        atomic_json(output / "watersheds.geojson", geojson)
        # This separate display geometry is simplified only for browser drawing.
        # All numerical results and the complete GeoJSON use original geometry.
        report["map"] = {"crs": grid["crs"], "bbox": list(domain.bounds), "features": [
            {"id": z.id, "name": z.name,
             "geometry": mapping(z.geometry.simplify(math.sqrt(grid["cell_ha"] * 10000) / grid["coordinate_unit_to_m"] / 2, preserve_topology=True))}
            for z in zones]}
        report["completed_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        report["rasters"] = {"study_area_fraction": fraction_path.name,
                             "transitions": {k: p.name for k, p in paths.items()}} if options.write_rasters else {}
        if temporal_paths:
            report["rasters"]["timeline"] = {key: path.name for key, path in temporal_paths.items()}
        atomic_json(output / "ledger.json", report)
        atomic_json(output / "status.json", {"signature": signature, "state": "complete", "completed_tiles": len(windows), "total_tiles": len(windows)})
        return report


def run_native_workspace(workspace: Path | str, scenario_rasters: Mapping[str, Path | str],
                         output: Path | str, **kwargs) -> dict:
    """File-level adapter; preserve the original scenario writer and all inputs.

    Pass each original scenario's completed land-cover path explicitly. The original
    scenario_set.json is retained as a context hash, not reinterpreted or rewritten.
    """
    root = Path(workspace)
    contexts = [root / name for name in ("run_manifest.json", "grid.json", "scenario_set.json") if (root / name).is_file()]
    contexts.extend(kwargs.pop("context_files", ()))
    return run_ledger(RasterInput(root / "rasters" / "landcover.tif"),
                      {name: RasterInput(path) for name, path in scenario_rasters.items()},
                      root / "huc12.geojson", output, context_files=contexts, **kwargs)

# Land-cover scientific figures

The Land-cover **Prepare scientific report source** action now retains a native vector map and three numerical figures per selected comparison. They enter the existing Scientific Reports preview, PDF, HTML and editable selected-Study transfer through the original source recipe. The complete interactive ledger, all CSV/GIS outputs and every original source remain attached.

## What the figures show

The geography map contains every original reporting polygon, vertex and hole. It reads `ledger/zones-original.geojson` through the same maintained polygon reader used for the ledger, using `_landcover_zone_id` and `_landcover_zone_name`. Its per-polygon analysis areas must match the completed ledger. Standard metre-based analysis grids use their actual CRS in the map. A non-metre analysis grid has an explicitly declared EPSG:6933 display transformation, while all numerical quantities retain the original analysis CRS and area basis. The map has equal XY scale, projected-grid distance and grid north.

For every original comparison, three additional figures show:

1. **Unique study-area class areas.** Reference and comparison hectares come from the row and column sums of the complete original domain transition matrix. Open circles and filled squares preserve the two roles. Axis labels use NLCD codes; full class names and exact values remain in the figure-data file and report tables.
2. **Net change by land-cover group.** Every retained group appears in its original order. Positive values mean the comparison has more group area; negative values mean less. The zero reference line makes the sign clear. Group definitions and gain/loss/net values remain those of the completed reducer.
3. **Reporting-area coverage and change.** Every original polygon with both numerical values is plotted. The horizontal denominator is inside-grid polygon area; the vertical denominator is valid analysis support. The caption reports the complete count and unavailable count. Overlapping marks may represent multiple polygons. The complete data file retains all polygons, including unavailable quantities.

The unique-union summary and per-polygon values remain distinct. Overlapping polygons are never added to obtain the study-area union. Source-edition order and explicit original labels remain intact. All area values are hectares under the ledger's stated area basis; percentage panels retain their different denominators. Land-cover areas do not estimate pollutant exports.

## Retained files and reproducibility

`model/landcover_report_figures.py` consumes the already-copied original ledger inside a report-source directory. It opens no input raster and repeats no raster accounting. Its `prepare(directory, edition, report, labels, expected_implementation)` returns ordinary file descriptors, a figure-spec path and ordered figure selections.

Each completed source includes:

- `figures/landcover-figures.json`: the native scientific-figure specification, exact geometry bank, per-polygon geometry identities, original CRS/area metadata, and complete numerical drawing coordinates.
- `figures/landcover-figure-data.json`: every original class/group/polygon figure quantity, including unavailable entries.
- One complete SVG per figure, drawn at the same 511.2-point width through the existing native scientific renderer.
- Exact source bodies for the figure producer, original polygon reader, scientific renderer and projected map renderer under `implementation/`.

The source identity includes all four implementation hashes. Each new source uses producer edition `saved-landcover-report/2`; previous immutable sources remain readable through the unchanged `get` and catalogue paths. The shared map and statistical rendering code are unchanged.

The producer verifies the copied ledger identity, completed state, original comparison order and polygon inventory. It reconciles the transition sum with the original valid support, verifies the original polygon areas after reopening, and refuses changed implementation sources during capture. It retains its complete output through the existing report-source manifest and CAS import.

## Existing native continuation

Adopt this producer with its helper and component dependencies into the current annual-source or simulated-input Land-cover operation. Reuse its actual completed ledger ID; prepare this new immutable report source once. Use its returned source selection in the original Scientific Reports operation.

Inspect the geographic and numerical figures in the native PDF and HTML, then export the saved Scientific Report through the current selected-Study receiver. Reopen the retained report and original land-cover ledger in the restored project. The editable transfer keeps the new figure specification, SVGs, source code and original inputs automatically because they are ordinary recipe companions. Preserve the original operation and producing run/source IDs throughout.

"""Original geometry and completed-ledger quantities for Scientific Reports.

The native reducer remains authoritative. These figures read its completed
tables and original polygon input without opening rasters or repeating accounting.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from copy import deepcopy
import math
from pathlib import Path

from .common import atomic_bytes, atomic_json, describe_file, digest, file_digest, read_json, verify_file

EDITION = "landcover-scientific-figures/1"
SPEC = "figures/landcover-figures.json"
GROUP_LABELS = {
    "developed": "Developed", "forest": "Forest", "wetland": "Wetland",
    "cultivated_crop": "Crops", "pasture_hay": "Pasture/hay",
    "water": "Water", "shrub": "Shrub", "herbaceous": "Herbaceous",
}


def implementation():
    from . import landcover_ledger, scientific_figures, scientific_map_figures
    modules = {"landcover_report_figures": Path(__file__),
               "landcover_ledger": Path(landcover_ledger.__file__),
               "scientific_figures": Path(scientific_figures.__file__),
               "scientific_map_figures": Path(scientific_map_figures.__file__)}
    return {name: {"path": str(path.resolve()), "sha256": file_digest(path)}
            for name, path in modules.items()}


def _number(value, *, minimum=None):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(value):
        raise ValueError("Land-cover figure needs its original finite numerical quantity")
    if minimum is not None and value < minimum:
        raise ValueError("Land-cover figure quantity is below its original domain")
    return value


def _axis(label, unit, low, high, ticks=None):
    return {"label": label, "unit": unit, "domain": [low, high],
            "ticks": ticks if ticks is not None else [
                {"value": low + (high - low) * index / 4,
                 "label": format(low + (high - low) * index / 4, ".4g")}
                for index in range(5)]}


def _figure(key, title, caption, panel, source, **metadata):
    return {"id": key, "title": title, "caption": caption, "panels": [panel],
            "source": deepcopy(source), **metadata}


def _numerical(report, labels, source):
    """Keep every original polygon point and native common-support quantity."""
    zones = report["zones"]
    zone_ids = [zone["id"] for zone in zones]
    keys = report["scenarios"]
    rows = {(row["zone_id"], row["scenario"]): row for row in report["rows"]}
    if (len(set(zone_ids)) != len(zone_ids) or zone_ids.count("__domain__") != 1
            or len(rows) != len(report["rows"])
            or set(rows) != {(zid, key) for zid in zone_ids for key in keys}
            or set(labels) != set(keys)):
        raise ValueError("Scientific figures need every original polygon/alternative row")
    figures, retained = [], []
    codes = sorted(int(code) for code in report["classes"])
    for number, key in enumerate(keys, 1):
        prefix = "comparison-" + format(number, "04d")
        description = labels[key]
        domain = rows[("__domain__", key)]
        support = _number(domain["support"]["analysis_valid_ha"], minimum=0)
        before = {code: [] for code in codes}
        after = {code: [] for code in codes}
        seen = set()
        for transition in domain["transitions"]:
            a, b = transition["from_code"], transition["to_code"]
            if (a, b) in seen or a not in before or b not in after:
                raise ValueError("Original transition matrix has a repeated or unknown class")
            seen.add((a, b))
            hectares = _number(transition["ha"], minimum=0)
            before[a].append(hectares)
            after[b].append(hectares)
        before = {code: math.fsum(values) for code, values in before.items()}
        after = {code: math.fsum(values) for code, values in after.items()}
        if not math.isclose(math.fsum(before.values()), support, rel_tol=3e-9, abs_tol=1e-7):
            raise ValueError("Original class transitions differ from their common support")
        class_rows = [{"class_code": code, "class_name": report["classes"][str(code)],
                       "baseline_ha": before[code] if support else None,
                       "comparison_ha": after[code] if support else None} for code in codes]
        height = max([*before.values(), *after.values(), 0.0])
        panel = {"title": "Unique study-area class areas",
                 "x": _axis("NLCD class code", "", -.7, len(codes) - .3,
                            [{"value": i, "label": str(code)} for i, code in enumerate(codes)]),
                 "y": _axis("Common-support area", "ha", 0, height * 1.08 if height else 1),
                 "series": [
                     {"geometry": "scatter", "label": "Reference", "marker": "circle-open",
                      "points": [{"x": i - .13, "y": before[code]} for i, code in enumerate(codes)] if support else []},
                     {"geometry": "scatter", "label": "Comparison", "marker": "square",
                      "points": [{"x": i + .13, "y": after[code]} for i, code in enumerate(codes)] if support else []},
                 ]}
        figures.append(_figure(prefix + "-classes", "Land-cover class areas", description +
            ". Areas are row/column sums of the original unique-union transition matrix on its "
            "selected common support. Reference is an open circle; comparison is a filled square. "
            "Full class names and exact values are retained in the figure-data file. " +
            ("The comparison has no supported area; class quantities are unavailable." if not support else ""),
            panel, source, scenario=key))
        groups = list(domain["groups"])
        group_rows, points = [], []
        for index, group in enumerate(groups):
            values = domain["groups"][group]
            row = {"group": group, **deepcopy(values)}
            group_rows.append(row)
            if values["net_ha"] is not None:
                points.append({"x": index, "y": _number(values["net_ha"]), "group": group})
        extent = max([abs(point["y"]) for point in points] + [0.0])
        extent = extent * 1.1 if extent else 1.0
        panel = {"title": "Unique study-area group change",
                 "x": _axis("Original class group", "", -.7, len(groups) - .3,
                            [{"value": i, "label": "G" + str(i + 1)} for i in range(len(groups))]),
                 "y": _axis("Comparison minus reference", "ha", -extent, extent),
                 "reference_lines": [{"axis": "y", "value": 0}],
                 "series": [{"geometry": "scatter", "label": "Net area change", "marker": "square", "points": points}]}
        group_key = "; ".join("G" + str(i + 1) + " " + GROUP_LABELS.get(group, group.replace("_", " "))
                              for i, group in enumerate(groups))
        figures.append(_figure(prefix + "-groups", "Net change by land-cover group", description +
            ". Positive values mean group gain; negative values mean loss on the selected common support. "
            "Groups retain the reducer's original definitions. " + group_key + ".",
            panel, source, scenario=key))
        polygon_rows, points = [], []
        for zone in zones:
            if zone["id"] == "__domain__":
                continue
            row = rows[(zone["id"], key)]
            coverage, changed = row["analysis_coverage_pct"], row["changed_pct_of_analysis"]
            original = {"zone_id": zone["id"], "zone_name": zone["name"],
                        "analysis_coverage_pct": coverage, "changed_pct_of_analysis": changed,
                        "analysis_valid_ha": row["support"]["analysis_valid_ha"],
                        "changed_ha": row["changed_ha"], "inside_grid_ha": zone["inside_grid_ha"]}
            polygon_rows.append(original)
            if coverage is None or changed is None:
                continue
            if any(not -.0000001 <= _number(value) <= 100.0000001 for value in (coverage, changed)):
                raise ValueError("Original coverage/change percentage is outside its numerical range")
            points.append({"x": coverage, "y": changed, "zone_id": zone["id"], "zone_name": zone["name"]})
        panel = {"title": "Every reporting polygon: support and change",
                 "x": _axis("Valid support / inside-grid area", "%", -.5, 100.5,
                            [{"value": i, "label": str(i)} for i in (0, 25, 50, 75, 100)]),
                 "y": _axis("Changed / valid support", "%", -.5, 100.5,
                            [{"value": i, "label": str(i)} for i in (0, 25, 50, 75, 100)]),
                 "series": [{"geometry": "scatter", "label": "Reporting polygon", "marker": "circle-open", "points": points}]}
        figures.append(_figure(prefix + "-support", "Reporting-area coverage and change", description +
            ". Each point is one original reporting polygon; overlapping marks can represent multiple polygons. "
            "The horizontal denominator is polygon area inside the raster, and the vertical denominator is "
            "that comparison's valid analysis support. " + str(len(points)) + " of " + str(len(polygon_rows)) +
            " polygons have both quantities; " + str(len(polygon_rows) - len(points)) +
            " with unavailable support remain in the complete data table. The unique-union row is separate. "
            "These percentages are land-cover quantities.",
            panel, source, scenario=key))
        retained.append({"scenario": key, "description": description,
                         "analysis_support_ha": support, "classes": class_rows,
                         "groups": group_rows, "polygons": polygon_rows})
    return figures, retained


def _geography(directory, report, source):
    from pyproj import CRS, Transformer
    from shapely.geometry import mapping
    from shapely.ops import transform as geometry_transform
    from .landcover_ledger import load_zones
    from .scientific_map_figures import positions
    original = directory / "ledger/zones-original.geojson"
    analysis_crs = CRS.from_user_input(report["grid"]["crs"])
    zones = load_zones(original, analysis_crs, id_field="_landcover_zone_id", name_field="_landcover_zone_name")
    original_rows = {row["id"]: row for row in report["zones"] if row["id"] != "__domain__"}
    if {zone.id for zone in zones} != set(original_rows):
        raise ValueError("Original map polygons differ from the completed ledger")
    metre = (analysis_crs.is_projected and len(analysis_crs.axis_info) >= 2
             and all(abs(axis.unit_conversion_factor - 1.0) <= 1e-12 for axis in analysis_crs.axis_info[:2]))
    # The maintained map renderer uses projected metres. Non-metre analysis CRSs
    # get a separately declared display projection; original accounting is kept.
    display_crs = analysis_crs if metre else CRS.from_epsg(6933)
    transform = None if metre else Transformer.from_crs(analysis_crs, display_crs, always_xy=True).transform
    source_file = describe_file(directory, original)
    geometries, layers, rows = {}, [], []
    xmin = ymin = math.inf
    xmax = ymax = -math.inf
    factor = _number(report["grid"]["coordinate_unit_to_m"], minimum=0) ** 2 / 10000
    for zone in zones:
        calculated = zone.geometry.area * factor
        if not math.isclose(calculated, original_rows[zone.id]["geometry_ha"], rel_tol=3e-9, abs_tol=1e-7):
            raise ValueError("Reopened original polygon area differs from its ledger")
        geometry = mapping(zone.geometry if transform is None else geometry_transform(transform, zone.geometry))
        # Normalize tuples exactly once for the native immutable JSON geometry bank.
        import json
        geometry = json.loads(json.dumps(geometry, allow_nan=False))
        key = digest(geometry)
        geometries[key] = geometry
        vertices = 0
        for point in positions(geometry):
            xmin, ymin = min(xmin, point[0]), min(ymin, point[1])
            xmax, ymax = max(xmax, point[0]), max(ymax, point[1])
            vertices += 1
        for role in ("contribution", "receptor"):
            layers.append({"geometry": key, "role": role, "receptor_id": zone.id, "source": source_file})
        rows.append({"zone_id": zone.id, "zone_name": zone.name, "geometry": key,
                     "vertices": vertices, "analysis_geometry_ha": original_rows[zone.id]["geometry_ha"]})
    span = max(xmax - xmin, ymax - ymin)
    if not math.isfinite(span) or span <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Original reporting geometry needs a positive display extent")
    margin = span * .04
    panel = {"kind": "projected_geometry_map", "title": "Original reporting polygons",
             "bounds": [xmin - margin, ymin - margin, xmax + margin, ymax + margin],
             "crs": {"name": display_crs.to_string(), "wkt": display_crs.to_wkt(), "units": "metre", "axes": "XY"},
             "layers": layers, "legend": [],
             "role_labels": {"contribution": "Reporting polygons", "receptor": "Original polygon boundaries"}}
    caption = (str(len(zones)) + " original reporting polygons, with every vertex and hole retained. "
               "The original ledger reader transforms the retained input to its analysis CRS; "
               "the reopened polygon areas match the saved ledger. " +
               ("The map uses that same projected grid." if metre else
                "The map is separately displayed in EPSG:6933; all area quantities retain the original analysis CRS.") +
               " The map identifies geographic scope; it does not encode change, pollutant export or flow direction. "
               "Original IDs, names, per-polygon geometry and source hashes remain in the retained specification.")
    figure = _figure("reporting-geography", "Original reporting geography", caption, panel, source,
                     geometries=geometries, polygons=rows,
                     analysis_crs=analysis_crs.to_wkt(), display_crs=display_crs.to_wkt(),
                     source_crs=read_json(original).get("crs"))
    return figure


def prepare(directory, edition, report, labels, expected_implementation):
    """Retain native vector figures alongside the already-copied original ledger."""
    from reportlab import Version as reportlab_version
    from reportlab.graphics import renderSVG
    from . import scientific_figures
    directory = Path(directory)
    implementation_now = implementation()
    if {key: value["sha256"] for key, value in implementation_now.items()} != expected_implementation:
        raise ValueError("Land-cover figure implementation changed after source selection")
    for name, descriptor in implementation_now.items():
        data = Path(descriptor["path"]).read_bytes()
        from hashlib import sha256
        if sha256(data).hexdigest() != descriptor["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Land-cover figure source changed during capture")
        atomic_bytes(directory / "implementation" / (name + ".py"), data, immutable=True)
    ledger = describe_file(directory, directory / "ledger/results/ledger.json")
    if read_json(directory / ledger["path"]) != report:
        raise ValueError("Scientific figures need the exact already-retained numerical ledger")
    if report.get("complete") is not True or edition.get("signature") != report.get("signature"):
        raise ValueError("Choose the completed original land-cover edition")
    figures, values = _numerical(report, labels, ledger)
    figures.insert(0, _geography(directory, report, ledger))
    data_path = "figures/landcover-figure-data.json"
    atomic_json(directory / data_path, {"schema": "upstate.landcover-figure-data/v1",
        "ledger_id": edition["id"], "signature": report["signature"], "ledger": ledger,
        "area_basis": report["grid"]["area_basis"], "support_scope": report["options"]["support_scope"],
        "comparisons": values}, immutable=True)
    spec = {"schema": "upstate.scientific-figure-spec/v1", "edition": EDITION,
            "title": edition["title"], "ledger_id": edition["id"], "signature": report["signature"],
            "implementation": expected_implementation,
            "rendering": {"reportlab_version": reportlab_version, "width_points": 511.2},
            "figure_data": describe_file(directory, directory / data_path), "figures": figures}
    atomic_json(directory / SPEC, spec, immutable=True)
    files = [describe_file(directory, directory / path) for path in (SPEC, data_path)]
    selections = []
    for figure in figures:
        drawings = scientific_figures.panel_drawings(figure, 511.2)
        if len(drawings) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Each saved land-cover figure needs one complete native panel")
        path = "figures/" + figure["id"] + ".svg"
        svg = renderSVG.drawToString(drawings[0])
        atomic_bytes(directory / path, svg.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(svg, str) else svg, immutable=True)
        files.append(describe_file(directory, directory / path))
        selections.append({"id": figure["id"], "path": path})
    files.extend(describe_file(directory, directory / "implementation" / (name + ".py"))
                 for name in sorted(implementation_now))
    for descriptor in files:
        verify_file(directory, descriptor)
    return {"figure_spec": SPEC, "figures": selections, "files": files,
            "summary": {"figure_count": len(figures), "comparisons": len(values),
                        "reporting_polygons": len(report["zones"]) - 1}}

"""Prepare or reopen an original land-cover ledger in Scientific Reports."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from . import landcover_report_source as report_source
from .workspace import Workspace


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--workspace", required=True, type=Path)
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    prepare = commands.add_parser("prepare", help="Retain the selected original ledger as a report source")
    prepare.add_argument("--ledger-id", required=True)
    prepare.add_argument("--title")
    inspect = commands.add_parser("inspect", help="Verify and reopen an imported report-source receipt")
    inspect.add_argument("--id", required=True)
    listing = commands.add_parser("list", help="List completed report-source receipts")
    listing.add_argument("--ledger-id")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    workspace = Workspace(args.workspace.resolve(), create=False)
    if args.command == "prepare":
        spec = {"ledger_id": args.ledger_id}
        if args.title is not None:
            spec["title"] = args.title
        value = report_source.prepare(workspace, spec)
    elif args.command == "inspect":
        value = report_source.get(workspace, args.id)
    else:
        value = report_source.list_sources(workspace, args.ledger_id)
    print(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Saved land-cover comparisons in Scientific Reports

Open a completed **Land-cover changes** edition and choose **Prepare scientific report**. Once the source is ready, **Open Scientific Reports composer** opens the existing Scientific Reports composer. Combine it with retained water-quality, receiving-water or conservation sources in the desired order. The composer produces its ordinary saved PDF, HTML, figures and original source package.

The source uses the original completed ledger. It retains the interactive land-cover report, all summary/support/group/transition CSVs, the full numerical JSON, transition and polygon-fraction GeoTIFFs, original selected polygon geometry and properties, original input binding and complete land-cover report ZIP. The original raster source bodies and declared companions remain attached. Native-run mode additionally retains the actual run raster dependencies verified against the computed ledger's input hashes.

## What the report means

The baseline and each alternative keep their selected order and original titles. Retained annual-source labels use the source's own vintage string and band selection. Run-based comparisons use the original saved scenario title and run ID. No calendar years are inferred.

Areas are the existing reducer's fractional polygon/pixel intersections in the reported CRS. The report repeats the original area basis and projection method. Equal-area remains the normal regional choice; a deliberately selected projected planar analysis, such as the simulated EPSG:26917 teaching case, retains that exact label.

The unique study-area union appears once. Each original reporting polygon appears in the complete watershed inventory and comparison tables. Overlapping polygon rows must not be summed into the union. Full original geometry is attached separately from the existing browser display geometry.

The saved support choice remains explicit:

- `all`: every comparison uses the common supported pixels across the reference and every selected alternative.
- `pair`: each reference/alternative comparison has its own supported intersection.

The report presents raster-valid, supported-class, pairwise-valid and selected-analysis areas separately. Reference-only, alternative-only, neither-supported, excluded-by-other-alternatives and unknown-class areas are retained. A change quantity with no analysis support stays unavailable. Changes are land-cover areas; modeled nitrogen, phosphorus and sediment values belong to their original separate model reports.

The unique-union section includes every changed-class transition and the original group gains, losses and net changes. The watershed tables include every original polygon. Complete per-polygon transition detail remains in the original CSV, JSON and interactive report, linked from the composed report. Display tables format numeric values for reading; the retained numerical JSON and CSV preserve the original exported quantities.

## Native source interface

Use the same existing application and Workspace that own the completed ledger:

```python
from model import landcover_report_source, observed_report_render
from model.workspace import Workspace

ws = Workspace(original_workspace, create=False)
source = landcover_report_source.prepare(ws, {
    "ledger_id": original_completed_ledger_id,
})
preview = observed_report_render.prepare(
    ws, [source["source"]], title=source["title"],
)
report = observed_report_render.render(ws, preview, new_report_directory)
reopened_source = landcover_report_source.get(ws, source["id"])
```

`prepare` accepts only `ledger_id` and optional nonempty `title`. It verifies the existing ledger through `landcover_workspace.inspect`, copies its original files and imports a normal `OBSERVED_CONTEXT` document. It creates no new land-cover or hydrology execution. Its return value contains `id`, `ledger_id`, `title`, `source`, `observed_binding`, `files` and `members`. All descriptors in the returned receipt are relative to `ws.root`.

`list_sources(ws, ledger_id=None)` returns completed source summaries. `get(ws, id)` verifies the receipt, project, every retained member, original imported recipe and exact observed-context binding. A repeated identical preparation reopens its completed source. A changed producer or original edition creates a new source identity and leaves previous editions intact.

The command-line entry point uses those same functions:

```sh
python -B -m model.landcover_report_source_cli --workspace /actual/workspace prepare --ledger-id ACTUAL_COMPLETED_LEDGER_ID
python -B -m model.landcover_report_source_cli --workspace /actual/workspace list --ledger-id ACTUAL_COMPLETED_LEDGER_ID
python -B -m model.landcover_report_source_cli --workspace /actual/workspace inspect --id ACTUAL_REPORT_SOURCE_ID
```

Use the real returned IDs. The source is saved under `landcover-report-sources/<source-id>`. Its ordinary `sources.json` and `landcover-report-source.zip` can carry the exact original report document and companions to another Workspace; the receiving source collection retains its own imported identity. In that case the Scientific Reports composer consumes the receiving source choice. The old project-local source receipt is reopened only with its original complete project.

## Original-data receiving and complete project transfer

Continue the already accepted annual or native-demo operation after its ledger completes. Prepare this source from that ledger ID, reopen it, then render through the existing Scientific Reports composer. Return the actual source ID, collection/document choice, completed report operation and generated PDF/HTML descriptors.

To continue the same native report through the application's ordinary complete archive:

```python
received = observed_report_render.archive_report(
    ws, new_report_directory, report, new_project_archive,
    new_independent_restore_directory,
)
```

Use distinct paths outside the active application and Workspace. The existing receiver verifies the complete archive inventory, project identity, original source selection and restored report files. The archive includes the original land-cover edition, its imported input collections, newly prepared report source and saved scientific report. Existing land-cover CLI receiving can independently inspect the original ledger through the restored application's own interpreter command.

The additive component depends on the maintained land-cover source adapter and Scientific Reports components. The current Land-cover installer carries the model, provider, descriptor, UI and guide together while preserving the installed shared route policy.


## Export this report as an editable selected Study

A saved Scientific Report can be selected in the existing **Study transfer**
workflow. When one of its ordered sources is a land-cover ledger from this same
project, the original source resolver includes:

- The complete original land-cover edition, input binding and declared outputs.
- Its retained reducer database and checkpoints, with ordinary concurrent-file
  and directory checks performed by Study transfer.
- The complete prepared report-source receipt, imported source document and its
  original companions.
- The exact raster and polygon source collections for annual-source mode.
- The exact original prepared grid, scenarios, profiles and selected run
  dependencies for retained-run mode, using the existing native run visitor.

The restored project keeps the ledger's original ID. Open **Land-cover changes**
and select that edition, or use the original Workspace CLI's inspect command.
The copied application and original source collections allow the normal source
reader to rehydrate its view when the ledger opens. Transfer itself reads raw CAS
objects and original records; it does not reconstruct source views or execute
geospatial/model code.

The lineage record distinguishes an original source produced by this same
project from one imported from another project. An external report source keeps
its contained original inputs, outputs and source identities. It does not bind
those identities to coincidentally matching local ledger or run paths.

The dispatcher calls `landcover_study_transfer.include_source` only for sources
explicitly ordered in a saved Scientific Report. Generic source traversal and
older unrelated Study selections retain their original contracts. The helper,
its dependency declaration and the maintained ScientificReport resolver join
must be installed together. The additive fragment also includes the helper in
`study-transfer` itself, so a report exporter does not depend on selecting the
Land-cover desk. That addition introduces no reverse component dependency.
Full Workspace backup remains available through the
original separate archive path described above.

### Same-operation receiving

After the existing native course produces the land-cover report source and its
saved ScientificReport edition, use that actual report ID in the existing Study
transfer selection. Keep the returned original project/transfer/report/ledger
IDs. Export and restore through the maintained Study APIs, then reopen both the
saved report and the original land-cover ledger in the restored application.

The resulting Study lineage retains the original source-body SHA, complete member
SHA inventory, input mode, selected operands and bands, native area basis and
fractional polygon-overlap method. A later unrelated run stage may complete;
the original captured land-cover raster descriptor and its bytes must still
match. Missing or differing original producing records surface before packaging.

## Geographic and numerical figures

Newly prepared report sources also contain the full original reporting-polygon map and three native vector figures for each selected comparison: unique-union class areas, signed group changes, and per-polygon support/change coverage. The completed ledger remains the numerical authority; each percentage retains its original denominator and every unavailable quantity remains in the attached figure data. The existing PDF and HTML composer consumes the retained specification and SVGs.

See [Land-cover scientific figures](LANDCOVER_REPORT_FIGURES.md) for the full figure definitions, original geometry and implementation identities, output inventory and same-operation receiving course. Existing immutable report sources and their editable Study lineage remain readable.

"""Retain a completed land-cover ledger for the existing Scientific Reports composer.

All numerical tables consume the original computed ledger. Input rasters,
reporting geometry and the original interactive/export products remain attached.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from copy import deepcopy
import json
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import tempfile
import zipfile

from . import landcover_workspace, observed_context
from .landcover_exports import _source_edition_rows
from .common import (atomic_json, describe_file, digest, file_digest, held,
                     identifier, now, read_json, verify_file)
from .reuse import copy_verified, destination_file

SCHEMA = "upstate.landcover-report-source/v1"
EDITION = "saved-landcover-report/2"
DIRECTORY = "landcover-report-sources"


def _copy(value):
    return deepcopy(value)


def _title(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
        raise ValueError("Supply a scientific report source title")
    return value.strip()


def _relative(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str) or "\\" in value or "\0" in value:
        raise ValueError("Retained report members need canonical relative names")
    path = PurePosixPath(value)
    if (path.is_absolute() or not path.parts or any(p in (".", "..") for p in path.parts)
            or path.as_posix() != value):
        raise ValueError("Report source members must remain inside their source")
    return path.as_posix()


def _same_file(actual, expected):
    return all(actual.get(key) == expected.get(key) for key in ("bytes", "sha256"))


def _text(value):
    if value is None:
        return "Not available"
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "Yes" if value else "No"
    if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False)
    if isinstance(value, float):
        return format(value, ".10g")
    return str(value)


def _table(columns, rows):
    return {"kind": "table", "columns": list(columns),
            "rows": [[_text(cell) for cell in row] for row in rows]}


def _links(items):
    return {"kind": "links", "items": [
        {"title": title, "path": _relative(path)} for title, path in items
    ]}


def _original_sources(workspace, binding):
    references = [binding["zones"]["selection"]]
    if binding["selection"].get("input_mode") in ("sources", "timeline"):
        references.extend(item["source_selection"] for item in binding["operands"])
    originals = {}
    for choice in references:
        key = (choice["source_collection_id"], choice["source_id"])
        if key not in originals:
            unused, entry = workspace.source_file(*key)
            originals[key] = {"source_collection_id": key[0], "source_id": key[1],
                              "entry": _copy(entry)}
    return [originals[key] for key in sorted(originals)]


def _run_members(workspace, binding, report):
    """Retain native run raster members using their current original Workspace paths."""
    if binding["selection"].get("input_mode") in ("sources", "timeline"):
        return []
    import rasterio
    accepted = {(item["bytes"], item["sha256"]) for item in report["inputs"]
                if item["role"] == "baseline" or item["role"].startswith("scenario:")
                or item["role"] == "raster-companion"}
    members = {}
    for operand in binding["operands"]:
        path = verify_file(workspace.root, operand["raster"])
        with rasterio.open(path) as dataset:
            paths = list(dataset.files)
        if str(path) not in paths:
            paths.append(str(path))
        for name in paths:
            actual = Path(name).resolve(strict=True)
            if not actual.is_relative_to(workspace.root.resolve()):
                raise ValueError("A native land-cover member is outside its retained Workspace")
            item = describe_file(workspace.root, actual)
            if (item["bytes"], item["sha256"]) not in accepted:
                raise ValueError("Native raster bytes differ from the original computed ledger")
            members[item["path"]] = item
    return [members[name] for name in sorted(members)]


def _operands(binding, report):
    source_rows = _source_edition_rows(report)
    if source_rows:
        editions = report["source_editions"]
        return editions["baseline"], {row["key"]: row for row in editions["alternatives"]}
    values = []
    for index, operand in enumerate(binding["operands"]):
        values.append({"key": "baseline" if index == 0 else operand["run_id"],
                       "label": operand["scenario"].get("title") or operand["run_id"],
                       "source_time": "Saved native land-cover operand",
                       "source_id": operand["run_id"], "source_collection_id": "",
                       "source_uri": "workspace://runs/" + operand["run_id"],
                       "band": 1, "raster": operand["raster"]})
    if [item["key"] for item in values[1:]] != report["scenarios"]:
        raise ValueError("Original run operands differ from the saved ledger order")
    return values[0], {row["key"]: row for row in values[1:]}


def _sections(edition, binding, report, originals):
    baseline, alternatives = _operands(binding, report)

        raise ValueError("The completed ledger row inventory differs from its zones and alternatives")
    if "__domain__" not in {zone["id"] for zone in report["zones"]}:
        raise ValueError("The completed ledger has no original unique study-area union")
    sections = [["Saved land-cover comparison", [
        "This report uses the completed land-cover ledger and its original reporting boundaries. "
        "The attached interactive report contains the geographic view and all class transitions. "
        "Areas measure categorical land-cover change; they do not estimate runoff or pollutant export.",
        _table(["Retained selection", "Value"], [
